messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — did a short bring-up of llama2-13b int8 on H100 across us-east/us-west/eu-west. p50s look fine, but eu-west p95 is ~2.8x higher when traffic goes through the edge-proxy-pop. wondering if it's routing + kernel mismatch or just cold-kv warmup

sam: Can you paste the numbers? also which kernel build and quant config?

maria: sure — quick summary from the smoke run (steady small prompts, 1-2 tokens/sec sim):

```
config: llama2-13b, int8-quant, batch=1, kv-cache-cache=true
hardware: H100 (driver:470.x), kernel: custom-kernel-v2 (attention fused)

region   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  tokens/s  notes
us-east  48       78       210       local edge-pop
us-west  52       83       200       local edge-pop
eu-west  55       220      190       routed via proxy-pop -> bigger tail
```

maria: raw traces show extra 70–150ms hop in eu-west path before it hits the H100 host. Not seeing CPU hot loops on the host side, looks network-ish or kernel fallback on that route.

oli: interesting. Could be kernel selecting non-fused attention due to slightly different sequence-length histogram or hop MTU. Did you collect kernel selection logs?

maria: yes, attached snippet below — on eu-west some requests fall back to generic-attn-path at step 1 (low probability but shows up at tail)

```
[select_kernel] seq_len=512 -> fused_attn (ok)
[select_kernel] seq_len=8   -> generic_attn (eu-west samples)
```

anya: If it's routing then we could A/B reduce proxy-pop weight for eu-west to see if p95 drops. Also assess capacity impact if we shift 20% of eu-west to us-east.

sam: What's the capacity delta if we prefer us-east? we need sizing numbers for dedicated pools.

maria: quick cap estimate (single H100 serving 13B int8 with our runtime):

```
mode: real-time batch=1
H100 peak qps(~1-token/req): ~220 req/s
p95 headroom target 99ms => safe qps per H100 ~170
So shifting 20% eu-west traffic (base 200 qps region) -> move 40 qps =~ 1/5 of H100 => add 1 H100 if you want full headroom, or accept 10-15% higher p95.
```

oli: To confirm kernel hypothesis: run a controlled canary where we force kernel v2 fused path on eu-west hosts and compare. If tail persists, it's routing/proxy-pop.

maria: plan: 1) re-run with kernel pin (force fused_attn) on a small canary in eu-west (5% traffic) 2) run a route bypass test sending traffic direct to host (bypass proxy-pop) 3) collect per-request routing hop times + kernel logs 4) share results here. Starting now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kernel-pin-canary -> eu-west-hosts (canary=5%) by maria (meta: ci/4567)

sam: please include the exact prompt set (10 seed prompts) and run both int8 and fp16 for comparison — sometimes quantized dispatch changes memory patterns that alter kernel decisions.

maria: good call. using seed set "tail-smoke-10" (will paste). Also running fp16 baseline. I'll post the after-run summary here (expect ~30–45min).

anya: If the bypass reduces p95 -> short-term mitigation is route-weight shift + follow-up infra ticket to fix proxy-pop path. We should also run a synthetic stress to check capacity sizing before shifting producers.

maria: noted. tagging infra to monitor network queue_depth on proxy-pop during canary. I'll update with measurements. thanks all — will post results.
